guarantees.claim: sub_word_in is assigned rot_word_out[0] when use_rot_word is true, otherwise rot_word_in[0]
When SecMasking is false, sw_in_mask is driven to all-zero

assumptions.claim: When SecMasking is false, external consumers of sw_in_mask must not interpret it as a valid mask share
assumptions.risk: Security masking scheme may be silently broken if sw_in_mask is used as a share

assumptions.claim: When SecMasking is true, the gen_no_sw_in_mask block is not present, so sw_in_mask must be driven by separate logic
assumptions.risk: sw_in_mask could become undriven or floating, causing X propagation

uncertain_points.claim: The comment 'Tie-off unused signals.' in the !SecMasking block suggests more signals should be tied off, but only sw_in_mask is assigned in the visible chunk
uncertain_points.risk: Floating or undriven inputs to other modules may cause metastability or simulation X mismatch
